text: Once upon a time there was a little child who wanted to repair something. He looked around and saw a kite in the sky. He was so excited! He ran to the kite and grabbed it. He was so happy to have a new kite. He ran back to the kite and put the kite in the sky. He watched it fly and it made him smile. He was so proud of his repaired kite. He was so happy that he had been able to repair it. He was so proud of himself. The end.

review.note: Child and kite are present, but repair is only asserted: the child grabs a flying kite and is then proud of repairing it. Positive resolution with The end and an inferred stop.

One day, the girl went to the park to play. She saw a cat. The cat was very pretty. The girl wanted to play with the cat. She tried to catch the cat, but the cat was too fast.
The girl was sad. She could not find the cat. The cat was gone. The girl went home with a bad ending to her day.

review.note: A girl sees a cat that escapes; her ownership of an already lost cat is not established. Sad return home and an inferred stop.

text:
Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a sandcastle. He was so proud of it that he wanted to show it to everyone. He ran to the sea and shouted, "Look at my sandcastle! It's so big and beautiful!"
The boy's mom smiled and said, "That's great! But don't forget to wash it away."
The boy was so excited that he ran back to the beach and started to wash his sandcastle. He was so proud of his work.
But then, something terrible happened. The sea started to get bigger and bigger.

review.note: Boy, castle and sea are present. The mother asks him to wash the castle and he is proud of doing so. The sea rises; destruction has not been shown. Open at the limit.
